intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GACR) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous (bi-allelic) mutation in the gene encoding ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) on chromosome 10q26.

paragraphs.text: Gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina is an autosomal recessive chorioretinal degeneration. It is caused by deficiency of the mitochondrial matrix enzyme ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) (Mitchell et al., 1988). Vision declines early in life and eventually leads to complete blindness (Balfoort et al., 2021). The disease also affects other systems: type 2 skeletal muscle fibers atrophy and contain tubular aggregates (Sipila et al., 1979), and the central and peripheral nervous systems are involved (Valtonen et al., 1999; Peltola et al., 2002).

paragraphs.text: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1983) described cataract in 9 phakic patients with gyrate atrophy. The lens opacities lay mainly along the confluence of the posterior sutures and interfered with vision because they were in the visual axis. In 3 cataractous lenses removed from patients aged 31 to 47 years, the posterior suture region was filled with liquefied, degenerated lens material typical of senile cataract. The authors found cataract to be a uniform finding by the second decade. They considered it distinct from the cataracts seen in other forms of retinal degeneration.

paragraphs.text: Valtonen et al. (1999) studied 23 untreated patients with gyrate atrophy, comparing them with age-matched controls and with 9 patients who had taken creatine or creatine precursor supplements for several years. Brain MRI showed degenerative white matter lesions in 50% of patients and premature atrophic changes in 70%, with a striking increase in the number of Virchow spaces. Of the patients who had an EEG, 58% showed abnormal slow background activity, focal lesions, or high-amplitude beta rhythm. The EEG findings were not associated with the MRI changes or with age or sex. MRI and EEG findings did not differ between supplemented and untreated patients.

paragraphs.text: Valle et al. (1980) put 1 patient on an arginine-deficient diet, which lowered plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limit of normal. Ornithinuria and lysinuria disappeared. Oral alpha-aminoisobutyric acid sped the fall by increasing renal ornithine loss. During 1.5 years on a diet of 10 to 20 g protein plus essential amino acids, plasma ornithine stayed between 55 and 355 microM, the chorioretinal degeneration did not progress, and vision apparently improved. Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (1980) reported that this diet lowered plasma ornithine fivefold over 20 months. After about 15 months, the electroretinogram, dark adaptation, and color vision improved, affecting rod function more than cone function.

checks.claim: Valle et al. (1980) put 1 gyrate atrophy patient on an arginine-deficient diet, which lowered plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limit of normal.
checks.evidence_quote: In one subject, an arginine-deficient diet led to progressive reduction in plasma ornithine from 13 times normal to the upper limits of normal
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: Ornithinuria and lysinuria disappeared in the gyrate atrophy patient on the arginine-deficient diet.

paragraphs.text: McInnes et al. (1981) gave a low-arginine diet to a 15-year-old patient with plasma ornithine of 0.6 to 1.2 mmol/l, lowering it to 0.15 to 0.25 mmol/l. After 5 weeks, visual function improved in 1 eye that had been severely impaired for 3 years. The improvement lasted until dietary compliance worsened at 8 months, after which vision regressed. Restricting arginine too far caused hyperammonemia, showing that arginine is an essential amino acid in OAT deficiency.

checks.explanation: The pretreatment ornithine range of 0.6 to 1.2 mmol/l matches the abstract.

checks.claim: The low-arginine diet lowered plasma ornithine in the 15-year-old gyrate atrophy patient to 0.15 to 0.25 mmol/l.
checks.evidence_quote: was given a low-arginine diet to reduce plasma ornithine to a concentration (0.15--0.25 mmol/l) near the normal range
checks.explanation: The on-diet ornithine range of 0.15 to 0.25 mmol/l matches the abstract.

checks.explanation: The 5-week timing, the single eye and the 3 years of impairment all match the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: Overrestriction of dietary arginine produced hyperammonaemia, indicating that arginine is an essential aminoacid in ornithine transaminase deficiency.
checks.explanation: OAT deficiency is the same condition as ornithine transaminase deficiency.

Visual fields did not constrict further, and fundus photographs showed slow worsening at an age usually associated with rapid progression.

paragraphs.text: Kaiser-Kupfer et al. (2002) followed 2 pairs of sibs treated with an arginine-restricted diet for 16 to 17 years. In each pair, the younger sib, who started the diet earlier, had slower progression of the chorioretinal lesions. The authors concluded that long-term reduction of ornithine started early may slow the lesions appreciably and slow the loss of retinal function to a lesser extent.

paragraphs.text: Balfoort et al. (2021) systematically reviewed 33 studies covering 107 patients. Treatments included protein-restricted diets, pyridoxine, creatine or creatine precursors, L-lysine, and proline. Protein-restricted diets lowered ornithine by 16.0 to 91.2%, and lysine supplementation lowered it by 21 to 34%. Pyridoxine responsiveness was reported for 30% of the mutations included. The studies were of low to moderate quality, and clinical effectiveness could not be established.

Studies in 1 human infant with gyrate atrophy also showed transient hypoornithinemia.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell et al. (1988) found a G-to-A transition that changed the OAT initiator codon from ATG (methionine) to ATA in 4 Lebanese patients from 2 pedigrees. They detected it by RNase protection and sequencing of PCR-amplified genomic DNA. The mutation segregated with the disease allele in both pedigrees. Translation starting at the nearest in-frame methionine was predicted to truncate OAT by 138 amino acids, removing the mitochondrial leader sequence and 113 amino acids of the mature peptide.

checks.evidence_quote: This mutation segregates with the GA allele in both pedigrees.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.
